title: The 1-2-3 Rule: When You Need an Alternate
hook: Do you legally need an alternate today? Count to three.

scenes.narration: You're filing to Kelso, E T A eighteen hundred Zulu. The TAF says fifteen hundred overcast, five miles, all afternoon. Pencil's hovering over the alternate box, kid. Fill it in, or not?
Fifteen hundred overcast, five miles, at your E T A. Alternate required — yes or no? Commit.

The test: one hour before to one hour after your E T A, at least two thousand foot ceilings AND three miles. Fifteen hundred fails the two thousand. You're filing an alternate. Why the two-hour window? Forecasts drift — the buffer absorbs their timing error.

The alternate has its own homework at your E T A: six hundred and two with a precision approach, eight hundred and two non-precision. No approach at all? The weather must let you descend from the M E A and land visually.
onScreenText: No IAP → descend from MEA, land VFR

scenes.narration: Cover the screen. The three numbers of the rule, and the two sets of alternate minimums. Go.
One hour either side. Two thousand. Three miles. Six-and-two, eight-and-two at the alternate. File one anyway, kid — an alternate is a prenup. Unromantic. Occasionally priceless.
And from last lesson — the five clearance items, in order. Don't make me say the acronym.
Ninety-one one sixty-nine. Read it before the examiner does.

quiz.question: Forecast at Kelso, ETA ±1 hr: ceiling 1,500 ft, visibility 5 SM. Alternate required?
choices: Yes — the ceiling is below 2,000 ft
quiz.explanation: You need BOTH ≥2,000 ft and ≥3 SM from 1 hour before to 1 hour after ETA. 1,500 ft fails, so file an alternate. (91.169)

quiz.question: Standard alternate minimums at an airport with only a VOR (non-precision) approach?
quiz.explanation: Standard alternate minimums: 600-2 precision, 800-2 non-precision, at the time of your ETA. (91.169(c))

quiz.question: Your alternate has no instrument approach at all. To list it, the weather must allow...
choices: Descent from the MEA, approach, and landing under basic VFR
quiz.explanation: With no IAP at the alternate, 91.169 requires ceilings/visibility allowing a descent from the MEA and a landing under basic VFR.
